key_insight: A 2D chiral fluid can be derived from classical Stokes hydrodynamics by a 90° rotational rule that pairs every standard stress/pressure/viscosity term with a chiral counterpart, enabling closed-form steady base states and cavity-flow predictions.
engineering_relevance: The framework gives engineers a compact constitutive model for predicting chiral active-fluid flows, including confined vortices and screening effects, with direct relevance to microfluidic and granular experiments.
method: Derive the full stress tensor and spin flux from angular-momentum conservation without assuming symmetric stress.
Use irreducible (deviatoric) decomposition so each classical transport channel maps to a rotated chiral partner with one coefficient per channel.
Solve the resulting modified Helmholtz–Poisson system for a circular cavity analytically and a square cavity numerically.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports closed-form solutions in a circular domain, numerical solutions in a square domain, and quantitative predictions intended for comparison with air-fluidised chiral-disk experiments.
watch_item: The model is specialized to steady 2D chiral fluids, so extension to 3D, strong transients, or more complex boundary conditions may require new constitutive assumptions.
paper_title: Steady base states in a two-dimensional chiral fluid. The chiral Stokes cavity
